notes: Kelly science review complete, 14 November 2026. Four proposed astronaut targets at recorded Curiosity waypoints. Local x/y use the shared southwest origin (west 8141000, south -287000), valid on both the archived 5 km crop and current 6 km app map. Order and stop_minutes are team planning estimates; channel-panorama is the optional bonus. All photos are nearby context views with unverified camera-to-stop offsets. Science readiness does not certify the traverse, rover drive, storm shelter or safety model.

stops.name: Mineral King Drill Site
stops.description: Proposed astronaut stop at Curiosity's sol 4102 waypoint near the Mineral King drill workspace beside Gediz Vallis. NASA reported successful drilling and sample analysis during the late-February 2024 Mineral King campaign. The nearby Mastcam image from sol 4107 shows the drill hole and tailings. Compare the bedrock context with material inside the channel; the waypoint is not a surveyed position of the drill hole or an astronaut sampling location.
stops.photo_caption: Nearby view. Curiosity Mastcam on sol 4107 shows the Mineral King drill hole and tailings during its February 2024 campaign. The stop is the sol 4102 rover waypoint, not a verified camera or drill-hole position. There is no separate sol 4107 waypoint in the supplied track, so the camera-to-stop distance is unverified.
stops.why: Compare bedrock near the Mineral King drill workspace with channel material to investigate how the local deposits differ.

photo_waypoint_bracket.note: Separation of rounded track waypoints only; not camera-to-stop distance or a bound.

stops.name: Sulfur Crystal Field
stops.description: Proposed astronaut stop at Curiosity's sol 4200 waypoint near the Whitebark Pass workspace in Gediz Vallis. On 30 May 2024 the rover crushed a rock whose yellow crystals were subsequently identified as elemental sulfur using APXS. NASA described this as the first discovery of pure sulfur on Mars. Mastcam photographed the Convict Lake fragments on sol 4208, 7 June 2024. Similar-looking light-toned rocks are not all independently confirmed as sulfur here; the source of the sulfur remains uncertain.
stops.photo_caption: Nearby view. PIA26309: Curiosity Mastcam on sol 4208 (7 June 2024) shows yellow elemental-sulfur crystals in the Convict Lake fragments, about 13 cm across. Colour is adjusted to Earth-like lighting. The stop uses the sol 4200 waypoint; the exact sol 4208 camera-to-stop offset is unverified.
stops.why: Document the elemental-sulfur discovery context and compare nearby light-toned rocks without assuming that every similar rock contains sulfur.

photo_waypoint_bracket.note: Separation of rounded track waypoints only; not camera-to-stop distance or a bound.

stops.name: Kings Canyon Drill Site
stops.description: Proposed astronaut stop at Curiosity's sol 4255 waypoint near the Kings Canyon drill workspace within the Gediz Vallis channel. The sol 4263 Mastcam image (3 August 2024) shows the drill hole. NASA's August campaign updates describe analysis of the drilled material, including delivery to SAM. Compare channel-floor material with bedrock outside the channel to investigate the deposits; this waypoint does not by itself establish the exact drill-block position or prove that a particular rock was carried down from higher ground.
stops.photo_caption: Nearby view. Curiosity Mastcam on sol 4263 (3 August 2024, 07:56:55 UTC) shows the Kings Canyon drill hole. The stop uses the sol 4255 waypoint. The supplied track has no separate sol 4263 waypoint, so the exact camera-to-stop distance is unverified.
stops.why: Compare channel-floor material near Kings Canyon with surrounding bedrock to investigate the origin and history of the deposits.

photo_waypoint_bracket.note: Separation of rounded track waypoints only; not camera-to-stop distance or a bound.

stops.name: Gediz Vallis Panorama
stops.description: Optional astronaut viewpoint at Curiosity's sol 4350 waypoint on its westward traverse away from Gediz Vallis. Use the nearby sol 4352 Mastcam panorama to compare the rocky channel-exit landscape and the buttes Texoli and Kukenán. The panorama was acquired on 2 November 2024 from an unverified camera position relative to this waypoint. This is a proposed context-photography stop, not a claim that the entire channel is visible or that a climb has been surveyed. Visit only if the return fits the team's time and safety checks.
stops.photo_caption: Nearby view. PIA26471: Curiosity Mastcam on sol 4352 (2 November 2024) while heading west away from Gediz Vallis. Two mosaics contain 171 and 169 frames taken around local midday; Texoli is at left and Kukenán at right. Colour is adjusted to Earth-like lighting. Black areas are mosaic gaps, not terrain or shadow measurements. The stop uses the sol 4350 waypoint; the exact camera-to-stop offset is unverified.
stops.why: Photograph the rocky channel-exit landscape and compare the Texoli and Kukenán butte views with Curiosity's panorama before returning.
